doc.button_a11y_keyboard: Executed using the Space or Enter keys.
doc.button_a11y_role: Uses the standard <button> element with role="button" automatically assigned.
doc.button_anatomy_container: Manages the button's boundary, padding, and rounded corners.
doc.button_anatomy_icon: Supplements the label. Can be placed before or after.
doc.button_anatomy_label: Text indicating the action. Centered alignment is standard.
doc.button_best_practice_1: In principle, limit to one Primary button per visual hierarchy or modal.
doc.button_best_practice_2: Use specific verbs for labels to help users predict the outcome of their action.
doc.button_check1: Does it convey the result (benefit) after clicking?
doc.button_check2: Are you avoiding generic words like "OK" or "Yes"?
doc.button_check3: Does the button make sense by itself without context?
doc.button_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate button type based on the context.
doc.button_choice_primary_when: The main action on the screen, or the single completion button.
doc.button_choice_secondary_when: Auxiliary actions, secondary options paired with Primary (Cancel/Back).
doc.button_choice_tertiary_when: Subtle or supplementary actions in dense UIs.
doc.button_click_area_desc:
Ensure the click area is large enough to prevent misclicks
Especially consider finger operations on mobile devices
doc.button_considerations_visibility_desc:
Make it stand out so users can find it quickly
Increase contrast between background and text
doc.button_consistency_desc:
Keep a consistent design for the same types of buttons to avoid user confusion
Recommended to use the same styles across the site
doc.button_design_intent: Buttons are the primary interface for users to explicitly perform actions (submit, save, delete, navigate) on a screen. Through visual weighting (Priority), they aim to smoothly guide the user to the next step.
doc.button_ex3_eg: When shortening "Save it" to "Save" to fit mobile footers
doc.button_feedback_desc:
Provide feedback upon clicking so users can confirm their action
Use color changes or animations
doc.button_guide_link: Guide: Refer to Guides / Link vs Button for when to use
doc.button_icon_after_desc: Used for actions with directionality like "Next" or "Submit" to express progression.
doc.button_icon_before_desc: The most common placement. Enhances visibility and visually supplements the action's meaning.
doc.button_icon_only_case_desc: Used for widely recognized features (Search, Settings, etc.) to achieve a clean look. Alternative text (aria-label) is required for accessibility.
doc.button_icons_only_desc:
Indicates a specific action
Use only if the icon is self-explanatory
doc.button_icons_with_text_desc: A button combining text and an icon
doc.button_ja_notes:
Notes on Languages:
Too polite expressions might drop visibility. Keep it concise.
doc.button_label_desc:
Use concise and clear words to convey what happens next
Example: Submit, Confirm, Cancel
doc.button_label_guidelines_desc: Use "Verbs" for button labels. This clarifies "what will happen" after clicking.
doc.button_meaning_desc:
Limit to around 3 colors to avoid confusion
Provide icons too, since color-blind users may not distinguish color alone
doc.button_noun_impact: May delay judgment of whether it is an action or a state
doc.button_primary_desc:
Indicates the main action, designed to stand out more than other buttons
Indicates the action you want users to take next
The most desired action on the screen
doc.button_scenario_form: Form Submission: Primary button placed at the bottom right of a modal.
doc.button_scenario_toolbar: Toolbar: Compact layout with icon-only buttons to save space.
doc.button_secondary_desc: Indicates an auxiliary action, designed to be less prominent than the primary button
doc.button_secondary_eg: "Cancel" (paired with primary, dialogue, major changes) or "Back", etc.
doc.button_size_desc_l:
Thumb-friendly size for mobile
Important buttons like CTA (landing pages) or Login
doc.button_size_desc_s:
Suitable size for mobile lists
In tables, sidebars, dense UIs, etc.
doc.button_state_active_desc:
Behavior when clicked
Conveys the pressing action
doc.button_state_disabled_desc:
Makes it inoperable
Conveys that it cannot be clicked
doc.button_state_focus_desc:
Behavior during keyboard operation
Conveys that it is the active target
doc.button_state_hover_desc:
Behavior when hovered
Conveys that it can be clicked
doc.button_state_loading_desc:
Makes it inoperable until processing finishes
Conveys it cannot be clicked until back to normal
Examples: "Loading...", "Processing...", "Saving..."
doc.button_states_desc: Unless intentionally animated, keep the size constant so layout shifts do not occur
doc.button_tertiary_desc:
Appears broken when placed next to primary/secondary without a background
Provides a clear click area when the background is shown
Like a "Text Link" or a "Ghost Button" where the background appears only on hover
doc.button_tertiary_eg: "Edit", "Cancel" (minor changes), "Link to submenu", "Help", "Share to SNS", "Add new", "Upload photo", "See details", etc.
doc.button_tokens_desc: Uses design tokens for background color, text color, borders, and spacing. Major tokens include --wim-color-primary, --wim-spacing-md, --wim-radius-md, etc.
doc.button_var_pri_dest_act: Particularly dangerous operations (Account deletion, clear all data)
doc.button_var_pri_dest_desc: Stands out the most, strongly warning the user "Are you sure?".
doc.button_var_sec_dest_act: General deletions (Remove one from list, delete a message, etc.)
doc.button_var_sec_dest_desc:
Not too prominent but still indicates "dangerous action"
Adjust size to fit properly with border thickness
doc.button_var_ter_dest_act: Subtle deletions (Delete at the corner of settings, minor clear)
doc.button_var_ter_dest_desc: When you don't want it to interfere with other options, but want to alert the user when noticed.
doc.button_variations_desc: Ensure button height remains the same across variations
doc.button_verb_impact: Purpose is clear at a glance
doc.buttongroup_a11y_spec: Assign role="group" to the container and set an aria-label to explain the purpose. Each button must be keyboard accessible.
doc.buttongroup_anatomy_buttons: Each element in the group. In joined mode, they share boundaries.
doc.buttongroup_anatomy_container: Holds the buttons and defines the outer frame and background.
doc.buttongroup_basic_desc: Places buttons horizontally. You can adjust the spacing using the gap property.
doc.buttongroup_best_practice_1: Group only related actions together; unrelated actions should be separate buttons.
doc.buttongroup_best_practice_2: Avoid using primary variant for all buttons in a group — use secondary or tertiary to reduce cognitive load.
doc.buttongroup_choice_group_when: When multiple actions are closely related (e.g., Undo/Redo, Align Left/Center/Right) and you want to visually unify them.
doc.buttongroup_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on the relevance of actions and the visual weight on the UI.
doc.buttongroup_choice_segmented_when: When presenting mutually exclusive options (tabs-like behavior) and wanting to maintain the current selection state.
doc.buttongroup_choice_single_when: When each action is independent and has a different context.
doc.buttongroup_design_intent: Grouped buttons present a set of parallel actions or related options. By visually joining them, you communicate to the user that they are a single logical group.
doc.buttongroup_joined_desc:
Setting the joined property to true joins the buttons without gaps.
In this mode, the rounded corners of intermediate buttons are removed for a unified design.
doc.buttongroup_long_desc: The ButtonGroup component is used to group and display multiple buttons.
doc.buttongroup_override_desc:
By specifying the priority property, you can unify the priority of all buttons in the group.
Especially when using joined mode, mixed priorities can break the design.
doc.buttongroup_scenario_pagination: Pagination: Unifying Prev, Next, and page numbers into one set.
doc.buttongroup_scenario_toggle: Related action cluster: Joining List / Grid triggers as adjacent buttons. For a persistent exclusive selection, prefer ToggleGroup or SegmentedControl.
doc.buttongroup_scenario_toolbar: Editor Toolbar: Grouping decoration buttons like Bold, Italic, Underline.
doc.buttongroup_sizes_desc: Examples of placing Large, Medium, and Small buttons.
doc.buttongroup_ux_note_desc:
As a UI design principle, it is recommended to have only one primary button per screen (or context).
If you use priority="primary" for multiple buttons, it increases cognitive load.

When unifying a group, choose secondary or tertiary. primary is possible but should be done with care.
doc.copybutton_a11y_desc: The accessible name changes with state: it reads "copy to clipboard" before the click and "copied" after it, and the same text is what the tooltip shows, so the sighted and the announced label never diverge. That name is the only signal a screen reader gets — the icon swapping to a check mark and the intent turning green are purely visual. If you override aria-label, note that you replace both states with one fixed string and the confirmation is lost.
doc.copybutton_anatomy_content: The central icon or label that changes state when the content is successfully copied.
doc.copybutton_anatomy_root: The interactive trigger that manages the copy to clipboard logic and the temporary success state.
doc.copybutton_best_practice_1: Use CopyButton consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.copybutton_best_practice_2: Test CopyButton behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.copybutton_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Button better suits the use case.
doc.copybutton_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.copybutton_choice_self_when: When CopyButton functionality with standard options is required.
doc.copybutton_comparison_2: Ideal for copying code snippets or unique IDs.
doc.copybutton_comparison_desc: Unlike regular buttons, CopyButton automatically gives visual feedback (icons/messages) after copying.
doc.copybutton_design_intent: CopyButton provides a one-click mechanism to copy text to the clipboard, complete with immediate visual feedback (such as changing the icon to a checkmark) to reassure the user that the action was successful.
doc.copybutton_long_desc: Details and usage for the Copy Button component.
doc.copybutton_scenario_1: Code Snippets: Allowing developers to copy terminal commands or API keys with one click.
doc.copybutton_scenario_2: Referral Links: Enabling users to easily share their unique invite URLs from a profile page.
doc.floatbutton_a11y_desc: The accessible name is taken from aria-label, then from label when it is a string, and finally from the icon name. That last fallback is a trap: a floating button with only an icon and no label is announced as its icon identifier, so a screen reader reads something like "PlusIcon" instead of the action. Always pass a name that describes what happens, since a floating button has no surrounding text to borrow meaning from.
doc.floatbutton_anatomy_content: The central icon or label displayed within the floating trigger.
doc.floatbutton_anatomy_root: The fixed-position container that anchors the button to a specific viewport corner.
doc.floatbutton_auto_shrink_desc: Float buttons auto-shrink based on scroll.
doc.floatbutton_backtop_desc: Quickly return to the top of the page when scrolled down.
doc.floatbutton_basic_usage: Standard implementation of FloatButton, typically positioned in a fixed corner of the screen.
doc.floatbutton_best_practice_1: Use FloatButton consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.floatbutton_best_practice_2: Test FloatButton behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.floatbutton_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Button better suits the use case.
doc.floatbutton_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.floatbutton_choice_self_when: When FloatButton functionality with standard options is required.
doc.floatbutton_design_intent: FloatButton is used for primary, high-frequency actions that should remain accessible at all times, such as 'Create New', 'Support Chat', or 'Scroll to Top', regardless of the user's scroll position.
doc.floatbutton_extended_desc: Float buttons can have extended text.
doc.floatbutton_extended_sizes_desc: Extended Float buttons are also available in different sizes.
doc.floatbutton_fixed_pos_desc: Define precise fixed coordinates for the floating button.
doc.floatbutton_group_desc: Organize multiple related actions into a single floating container.
doc.floatbutton_long_desc: Details and usage for the Float Button component.
doc.floatbutton_menu_desc: Expands child buttons when clicked or hovered, saving screen space while offering multiple choices.
doc.floatbutton_scenario_1: Customer Support: Providing a persistent 'Help' or 'Chat' trigger at the bottom-right of every page.
doc.floatbutton_scenario_2: Quick Create: A 'New Post' button that stays accessible while browsing a social feed.
doc.floatbutton_sizes_desc: Float buttons are available in different sizes.
doc.floatbutton_tooltip_desc: Display a helpful description when hovering over the floating button.
doc.hamburgermenu_a11y_desc: The trigger carries aria-expanded reflecting the open state, and its accessible name changes with that state: it is announced as "open menu" when closed and "close menu" when open, taken from the translations unless aria-label is supplied. A name that changes with state is deliberate here — the icon alone is identical in both states, so a fixed name would leave a screen reader user unable to tell what pressing it will do.
doc.hamburgermenu_anatomy_content: The hidden navigation links or menu items that are revealed when the toggle is active.
doc.hamburgermenu_anatomy_root: The interactive 'three-bar' icon that serves as the toggle for the collapsible menu.
doc.hamburgermenu_best_practice_1: Use HamburgerMenu consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.hamburgermenu_best_practice_2: Test HamburgerMenu behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.hamburgermenu_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Sidebar better suits the use case.
doc.hamburgermenu_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.hamburgermenu_choice_self_when: When HamburgerMenu functionality with standard options is required.
doc.hamburgermenu_design_intent: HamburgerMenu is the industry-standard pattern for mobile navigation. It saves valuable screen real estate by tucking navigation links into a collapsible drawer or overlay, ensuring that the main content remains the focus on small devices.
doc.hamburgermenu_scenario_1: Mobile Headers: Consolidating secondary links on small screens to keep the UI clean.
doc.hamburgermenu_scenario_2: Responsive Apps: Switching from a sidebar to a hamburger menu on tablet viewpoints.
doc.iconbutton_a11y_desc: This is a thin wrapper around Button: it adds layout and styling and no ARIA of its own, so the roles, the accessible name and the keyboard behaviour all come from Button. Read that component's accessibility notes — anything required there is required here, and props you pass through reach it unchanged.
doc.iconbutton_anatomy_content: The central SVG icon that visually communicates the button's action.
doc.iconbutton_anatomy_root: The compact container that manages interaction states and ensures a consistent hit area.
doc.iconbutton_best_practice_1: Use IconButton consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.iconbutton_best_practice_2: Test IconButton behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.iconbutton_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Button better suits the use case.
doc.iconbutton_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.iconbutton_choice_self_when: When IconButton functionality with standard options is required.
doc.iconbutton_design_intent: IconButton is used for triggers that are globally recognized by icons (like 'close', 'edit', or 'delete') where space is limited. It provides a compact interface while maintaining the same interactive properties as a standard button.
doc.iconbutton_long_desc: A button component that displays only an icon.
doc.iconbutton_scenario_1: Table Actions: Providing 'Edit' and 'Delete' triggers in a dense data grid.
doc.iconbutton_scenario_2: Toolbar: Compact formatting triggers (Bold, Italic) in a text editor.
doc.iconbutton_title: A button component that displays only an icon instead of text.
doc.link_a11y_note_desc: Avoid ambiguous text like "Click here" or "Learn more". Instead, use specific descriptive phrases that clarify the destination (e.g., "View Pricing Plans"). This helps screen reader users understand where the link leads and strongly improves SEO.
doc.link_icons_desc: Icons can be placed on the left or right of the label.
doc.link_long_desc: The Link component provides text-based navigation or links to external resources. It supports internationalization, resizing, icon additions, and three levels of priority.
doc.link_priority_desc: Select from primary, secondary, or tertiary based on the link importance.
doc.link_priority_primary_desc: The most visible style. Used for primary actions like "View Pricing Plans".
doc.link_priority_secondary_desc: The standard text link style. Used for general navigation.
doc.link_priority_tertiary_desc: A subtle link style used for supplementary or lower-priority navigation items.
doc.link_priority_tertiary_style_desc: A subtle style with minimal decoration. Suitable for supplementary links or crowded areas.
doc.link_sizes_desc: Supports three sizes: small, medium, and large.
doc.link_vs_button_guide_desc: See Guides / Link vs Button for when to use `` vs `
doc.linkbutton_a11y_desc: This renders an anchor, so it is announced as a link and activates with Enter rather than Space — do not use it for actions that do not navigate. aria-label is passed straight through and has no fallback, so a link button rendered with an icon and no text has no accessible name at all. Give it one whenever the label is not visible text.
doc.linkbutton_anatomy_content: The text label or icon that indicating the navigation target.
doc.linkbutton_anatomy_root: The anchor-based container that inherits button styling while maintaining semantic link behavior.
doc.linkbutton_best_practice_1: Use LinkButton consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.linkbutton_best_practice_2: Test LinkButton behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.linkbutton_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Button better suits the use case.
doc.linkbutton_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.linkbutton_choice_self_when: When LinkButton functionality with standard options is required.
doc.linkbutton_design_intent: LinkButton is an anchor element styled to look like a standard button. It is intended for navigation-based actions (e.g., 'View Details', 'Go to Dashboard') where button-like visual prominence is desired but the underlying behavior is a URL transition.
doc.linkbutton_long_desc: A button component that functions as a link.
doc.linkbutton_scenario_1: CTA Sections: Promoting a 'Get Started' journey that leads to a signup page.
doc.linkbutton_scenario_2: Social Sharing: Providing 'View on GitHub' or 'Follow on Twitter' buttons in a footer.
doc.linkbutton_title: A button that functions like a link, used for navigation or actions that look like links.
doc.button_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the button. Space or Enter activates it. Disabled buttons are not reachable by keyboard.
doc.buttongroup_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the button group container. Each button within the group is individually focusable.
doc.copybutton_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the button. Enter or Space copies the target content to the clipboard.
doc.floatbutton_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the float button. Enter or Space activates it. When a group is open, Tab moves focus through each button in the group. Escape collapses the group.
doc.hamburgermenu_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the hamburger button. Enter or Space toggles the menu open or closed.
doc.icon_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction. Decorative icons should have aria-hidden="true". Meaningful icons should have an accessible label.
doc.iconbutton_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the button. Enter or Space activates it. Disabled buttons are not reachable by keyboard.
doc.link_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the link. Enter activates it. The link follows standard browser anchor navigation behavior.
doc.linkbutton_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the link button. Enter activates it. It behaves as a standard anchor element for keyboard users.
doc.dropdown_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the dropdown trigger. Enter or Space opens the dropdown. Arrow keys navigate options. Enter selects the focused option. Escape closes the dropdown.
doc.button_is_concise: Keep labels concise; prefer a single line by default.
doc.splitbutton_long_desc: A main action with a menu of related actions behind a toggle. Use it when one choice is right almost every time but a few near-neighbours have to stay reachable — Save with Save as draft behind it, Deploy with Deploy to staging.
doc.splitbutton_design_intent: The two halves take the same variant, intent and size, so they read as one control rather than two buttons that happen to touch. Styling them apart is not offered: the moment they diverge, the pair stops looking like a single thing.
doc.splitbutton_choice_matrix_desc: Pick by whether one action is clearly the default.
doc.splitbutton_choice_self_when: One action dominates and the rest are variations of it.
doc.splitbutton_choice_alt_no_default: None of them is a default.
doc.splitbutton_choice_alt_touch: A floating action button on touch.
doc.splitbutton_a11y_desc: The toggle half only shows a chevron, so it has no text to name it. toggleLabel is required by the type for that reason — a button with no accessible name is a WCAG failure, and the compiler is a better place to catch it than a test run. The menu comes from Dropdown, which owns the roving focus and Escape handling.
doc.splitbutton_keyboard_desc: Tab reaches the main action and the toggle as two stops. The toggle opens with Enter or Space; inside the menu, arrow keys move and Escape closes, all handled by Dropdown.
doc.splitbutton_scenario_1: A form footer where Save is what almost everyone wants, but Save as draft and Save and close must stay one click away.
doc.splitbutton_scenario_2: A deploy button where Deploy to production is the default and the other environments live behind the toggle.
doc.splitbutton_best_practice_1: Put the most-used action in the main half. If you cannot pick one, use Dropdown instead — a split button with an arbitrary default is worse than a plain menu.
doc.splitbutton_best_practice_2: Keep the menu short. Once it passes a handful of entries it is a menu with a button stuck to it, not a split button.
